The simplest alkyne, this colorless gas owes its straight-line shape to a carbon-carbon triple bond — and though pure it's odorless, commercial grades reek thanks to impurities. What is it?
Acetylene (systematic name: ethyne) is a chemical compound with the formula C2H2 and structure HCCH.
This Indian economist won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his work on welfare economics and has also studied the causes of famines — who is he?
Amartya Sen (born 3 November 1933) is an Indian economist and philosopher.
Found only on male deer, except reindeer, this branching structure of bone and cartilage falls off and regrows from scratch each year — what is it?
Antler are extensions of an animal's skull found in members of the Cervidae (deer) family.
Caused by poor circulation, lost nerve supply, or simple disuse, this process shrinks a cell, organ, or tissue below its normal mature size — what's it called?
Atrophy is the partial or complete wasting away of a part of the body.

Known only from larval and juvenile specimens until video footage of much larger adults surfaced, this deep-sea cephalopod genus holds its long, elbow-like arms perpendicular to its body — what is it?
Bigfin squid are a group of rarely seen cephalopods with a distinctive morphology.
This flowering plant family is known for flowers with four petals arranged in a cross shape, and includes crops ranging from leafy greens to root vegetables to condiment seeds. Name the family?
Brassicaceae (the older but equally valid) Cruciferae is a medium-sized and economically important family of flowering plants commonly known as the mustards, the crucifers, or the cabbage family.

Spread through contact with infected feces and capable of killing up to 91% of untreated cases, this highly contagious virus mainly strikes dogs and wolves but can also infect foxes, cats, and skunks — what's the virus?
Canine parvovirus (also referred to as CPV, CPV2, or parvo) is a contagious virus mainly affecting dogs and wolves.

The only living member of its genus, this big cat sprints at up to 104 km/h thanks to powerful hindlimbs, long legs, and a flexible spine, and wears black tear-like streaks down its face; which animal is it?
Cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is a species of large feline and the only living member of the genus Acinonyx.

Native to western South America, this shrub bears oval leaves and red berries, and when its leaves are chewed or brewed as tea they act as a mild stimulant with no evidence of addiction — which plant is it?
Coca refers to any of the four cultivated plants in the family Erythroxylaceae, native to western South America.
Native to North America and smaller than its close relative the gray wolf, this canine fills a similar ecological niche to the golden jackal of Eurasia — which animal?
Coyote (Canis latrans) is a species of canine also known as the American jackal, prairie wolf, and brush wolf.
Defined as having at least three loose or watery bowel movements in a day, this common condition can quickly cause dehydration, especially in children. What condition is it?
Diarrhea (American English), also spelled diarrhoea (British English), is the condition of having at least three loose, liquid, or watery bowel movements in a day.
This English physician created the world's first vaccine, targeting smallpox, and in doing so coined the very term 'vaccine' — derived from the Latin for 'pustules of the cow.' Who was he?
Edward Jenner (17 May 1749 - 26 January 1823) was an English physician and scientist who pioneered the concept of vaccines and created the smallpox vaccine, the world's first vaccine.
The major female sex hormone, this estrogen steroid drives the development of breasts and a female pattern of fat distribution and regulates the menstrual cycle — which one is it?
Estradiol (E2), also called oestrogen, oestradiol, is an estrogen steroid hormone and the major female sex hormone.

Sometimes mistakenly called a cat despite belonging to the weasel family, this North American forest-dwelling carnivore is the only living species in its genus and is larger than the martens it resembles — what animal is it?
Fisher (animal) (Pekania pennanti) is a carnivorous mammal native to North America, a forest-dwelling creature whose range covers much of the boreal forest in Canada to the northern United States.

The first person in Germany to hold a professorship dedicated to experimental physics, he is remembered for his posthumous 'waste book' notebooks and for the tree-like electrical discharge patterns named after him. Who is he?
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg (1 July 1742 - 24 February 1799) was a German physicist, satirist, and Anglophile.
This branch of medicine focuses on the female reproductive system, and when combined with the study of pregnancy and childbirth forms the field known as OB-GYN — name the specialty?
Gynaecology (or gynecology in American English) is the area of medicine concerned with conditions affecting the female reproductive system.

First described by an English physician in 1832, this cancer of the lymphocytes is identified by giant multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells in the lymph nodes, and about half its cases trace back to the Epstein-Barr virus. What is it?
Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a cancer where multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells (RS cells) are present in the lymph nodes.

Forming at or below zero degrees Celsius, this naturally occurring crystalline solid is technically classified as a mineral and appears on Earth, other planets, and even in interstellar space — what is it?
Ice is water that is frozen into a solid state, typically forming at or below temperatures of 0 C, 32 F, or 273.15 K.
Trained in biochemistry and physiology before ranging into geography and anthropology, this American author won the 1998 Pulitzer for Guns, Germs, and Steel — who is he?
Jared Diamond (born September 10, 1937) is an American scientist, historian, and author.

This childhood illness of unknown cause mainly affects kids under five, causing a prolonged fever lasting more than five days that doesn't respond to typical fever-reducing medicine, plus inflamed blood vessels throughout the body — name the syndrome?
Kawasaki disease (also known as mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome) is a syndrome of unknown cause that results in a fever and mainly affects children under 5 years of age.
With about 180,000 described species — roughly 10% of all known living organisms — which insect order is the second largest, trailing only the beetles?
Lepidoptera are an order of winged insects which include butterflies and moths.
Serving under Chancellor Adenauer, this economist championed West Germany's postwar economic miracle before becoming chancellor himself in 1963 — who is he?
Ludwig Erhard (4 February 1897 - 5 May 1977) was a German politician and economist who served as the second chancellor of West Germany from 1963 until 1966.
The heaviest and largest members of the squirrel family, these 15 species of grazing ground-dwellers vanish each winter to hibernate underground — what are they?
Marmot are large ground squirrels in the genus Marmota, with 15 species living in Asia, Europe, and North America.

An advanced modification of the Korean War-era MiG-15, this Soviet transonic fighter jet entered production in 1952, was license-built in both China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — what's the aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17 (NATO reporting name: Fresco) is a transonic fighter aircraft that was produced in the Soviet Union from 1952 and was operated by air forces internationally.
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this tiny bacterial species causes a form of atypical lung infection linked to cold agglutinin disease — which microbe first isolated as the 1944 'Eaton agent'?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
Sold in packs needing a desiccant to keep it from absorbing moisture, this seaweed sheet was once used as currency and shrine offerings in Japan — what is it?
Nori is a dried edible seaweed used in Japanese cuisine, usually made from species of the red algae genus Pyropia, including P. yezoensis and P. tenera.
Part of the Bovidae family, this genus of seven social species is better known simply as sheep, all thought to trace back to the wild mouflon — which genus?
Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.

Which American chemist was the first to synthesize physostigmine and pioneered making progesterone and testosterone from plant sterols — even starting a company to extract steroid intermediates from wild Mexican yams?
Percy Lavon Julian (April 11, 1899 - April 19, 1975) was an American research chemist and a pioneer in the chemical synthesis of medicinal drugs from plants.
This zodiac sign's Latin name means 'fishes,' and it's where the ecliptic crosses the celestial equator near the March equinox — which one?
Pisces (constellation) is a constellation of the zodiac. It is between Aquarius, of similar size, to the southwest and Aries, which is smaller, to the east.

Caused by a mutation in a single gene that holds the cell nucleus together, this rare disorder makes children age much faster than normal, with most patients living only into their teens or twenties — what's the condition?
Progeria (also Hutchinson-Gilford syndrome or Hutchinson-Gilford progeroid syndrome; HGPS) is a type of progeroid syndrome.

Cultivated mainly for its oil-rich seeds, this yellow-flowered Brassica crop is the source of a low-toxicity oil marketed under a Canadian-coined name, and ranks as the world's third-largest vegetable oil source — what is it?
Operating under a pseudonym borrowed from The Princess Bride, this American created the first modern darknet marketplace before his 2013 FBI arrest — who is he?
Ross Ulbricht (born March 27, 1984) is an American cybercriminal who created and operated Silk Road, the first modern darknet market, from 2011 until his arrest in 2013.
Most episodes of this brain-activity disruption last under two minutes and leave the person confused or fatigued afterward, but one lasting over five minutes is a medical emergency — what is it?
Seizure is a sudden disruption of brain activity caused by excessive, synchronized neuronal firing that results in changes in behavior.
With the formula Na2CO3, this odorless white salt yields an alkaline solution in water and earned the name 'soda ash' because plant ashes once gave it up. What is it?
Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.

Harvested from the seeds of the nux-vomica tree, this bitter colorless alkaloid is infamous as a poison for rodents and birds — yet was once doled out in tiny doses to stimulate the heart and bowels. What is it?
Strychnine (-nin, US chiefly -nyne) is a highly toxic, colorless, bitter, crystalline alkaloid used as a pesticide, particularly for killing small vertebrates such as birds and rodents.
A colorless, water-miscible cyclic ether and a versatile solvent, this compound is mainly used as a precursor to polymers and is an isomer of butanone — what is it?
Tetrahydrofuran (THF), or oxolane, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2)4O.

A phenylpiperazine compound in the serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor class, this antidepressant treats depression, anxiety and insomnia but carries a rare risk of prolonged, painful erections — which drug?
Trazodone is an antidepressant medication used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and insomnia.
Once classified in the honeysuckle family before molecular studies gave it its own, this genus of 150-plus shrub species reaches Africa only via the Atlas Mountains — which genus?
Viburnum is a genus of about 150-175 species of flowering plants in the family Viburnaceae.

This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under PM Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for opposing EU-imposed austerity, before co-founding the left-wing party DiEM25 — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis (born 24 March 1961) is a Greek economist, academic, author, and politician.
Also called sweet flag, this wetland plant contains psychoactive compounds and has been banned from American food products despite centuries of use in traditional medicine — which species?
Acorus calamus: Species of plant. Acorus calamus (also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root, among many other common names) is a species of flowering plant with psychoactive chemicals.
This congenital condition causes a total or partial absence of pigment, leading to white hair, pale skin, and often pink or reddish eyes — what is it called?
Albinism: Disorder causing lack of pigmentation.
Despite being named after a European bird for its reddish-orange breast, this thrush is the most abundant landbird on its continent, numbering some 370 million individuals — what is it?
American robin: Species of bird. The American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.

A German pharmacist coined this pigment's name from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue' in 1835 — it shifts red to purple to blue depending on pH and colors blueberries, black rice, and autumn leaves; what is it?
A notoriously toxic metalloid and pnictogen with atomic number 33, it's used in lead alloys for car batteries and ammunition and as a semiconductor dopant — which element is it?
Arsenic: Chemical element with atomic number 33 (As). It is a metalloid and one of the pnictogens, and therefore shares many properties with its group 15 neighbors phosphorus and antimony.
The world's largest nocturnal primate, this Madagascar lemur has ever-growing rodent-like teeth and taps tree trunks with a bony middle finger to fish out grubs by echo — which animal?
Aye-aye: Species of primate. This foraging method is called percussive foraging, and takes up 5–41% of the aye-aye's foraging time.
Named after a barberry-related plant genus and glowing bright yellow under ultraviolet light, this alkaloid was recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text around 200 BC. What compound is it?
This North American wild cat earns its name from the black-tipped, stubby tail it sports, along with distinctive black bars on its forelegs — one of the four species of lynx. Which animal is it?

A nerve compression syndrome caused when the median nerve in the wrist becomes compressed, causing numbness and tingling in the thumb and fingers. What is this condition?

Also known as silver beet or perpetual spinach, this leafy green shares its species with beetroot — which vegetable?

Sold under the brand name Celexa, this SSRI antidepressant treats major depressive disorder, OCD, panic disorder, and social anxiety — what is it?
Citalopram: SSRI antidepressant. Citalopram, sold under the brand name Celexa among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
This icy wanderer of the solar system grows a gassy halo and sometimes a tail stretching more than an astronomical unit as it nears the sun — what is it?
Comet: Natural object in space that releases gas.
Spread mainly through the fecal-oral route, these single-stranded RNA enteroviruses share traits with poliovirus and rank among the leading causes of aseptic meningitis — which pathogens?
Coxsackievirus: Virus that causes digestive upset and sometimes heart damage.

Driven by a gradient in chemical potential, this stochastic process describes the net movement of particles from areas of higher to lower concentration and can even reverse direction in spinodal decomposition — what physical process is this?
Diffusion: Transport of dissolved species from the highest to the lowest concentration region.
Sometimes nicknamed 'math dyslexia' even though it's a distinct condition, this learning disorder involves persistent difficulty understanding numbers and performing calculations — what is it called?

Comprising more than 700 species mostly native to Australia, these trees and shrubs have oil-gland leaves and a fused 'cap' of sepals and petals covering the stamens, inspiring their Greek-derived name?
This neurodegenerative prion disease has trouble sleeping as its hallmark symptom, most often stemming from a mutation in the PRNP gene — what is it?

Also known as reishi or lingzhi, this red-colored fungus grows on decaying hardwood in parts of Europe and China — what is it?

This general term covers any organ that secretes substances either straight into the bloodstream, like endocrine ones, or through a duct to a body surface, like exocrine ones — what type of structure is it?
Gland: Type of animal organ. A gland may also function to remove unwanted substances such as urine from the body.
Known to the British as the Martlet, this American carrier-based fighter entered service in 1940 and remained the U.S. Navy's best fighter against the Mitsubishi Zero until mid-1943 — which aircraft?

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: Enlargement of the heart muscle. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.
The global network of networks links private, public, academic, business and government networks using which protocol suite?

This Swiss psychologist's theory of cognitive development in children gave rise to a field he called genetic epistemology — who was he?

Native to Afghanistan and Iran, this herb tastes like an intensified cross between celery and parsley, with seeds used much like fennel — what is it?

Mandarin duck: Species of bird. The mandarin duck (Aix galericulata) is a perching duck species native to East and Northeast Asia.

A colorless gas with the formula NO, this free radical carries an unpaired electron and can be brewed by lightning in a thunderstorm. What molecule is it?

Named after the Greek word for tumor, first used this way by the physician Galen nearly two millennia ago, this medical field focuses on diagnosing and treating cancer — what is it called?

Nicknamed golden root or Arctic root, this Crassulaceae plant is popular in herbal supplements even though the FDA has warned sellers against overselling its health benefits — which plant?

Extremely cold-hardy and thriving in poor soil, this cereal grass is a staple grain behind Scandinavian crispbread and a certain whiskey style — what is it?
Rye: Species of grain. Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
Sitting near the center of the Milky Way between Libra and Sagittarius, this zodiac constellation's recognition predates ancient Greek culture — which constellation?

This Hungarian-American aerospace pioneer made crucial advances in supersonic and hypersonic airflow, and the agreed boundary of outer space — the "___ line" — bears his name. Who was he?

Marketed as Topamax, this oral medication treats epilepsy and prevents migraines, though it can cause weight loss and kidney stones as side effects — what is it?

Spread by body lice, chiggers, or fleas depending on the strain, this group of bacterial diseases causes fever, headache, and rash, and is treated with the antibiotic doxycycline — what is it?
Typhus: Group of infectious diseases. Typhus, also known as typhus fever, is a group of infectious diseases that include epidemic typhus, scrub typhus, and murine typhus.
Despite a scientific name meaning 'sand burrower,' this snake actually prefers rocky terrain and is considered Europe's most dangerous viper thanks to fangs up to 13mm long — which species?

In 1879 at the University of Leipzig, this German scholar founded the first formal psychology laboratory, earning him the title 'father of experimental psychology' — who is he?
